We’re introducing ChatGPT Wallet, setting a new bar for secure payments by agents. It’s the first wallet that lets agents pay without access to users’ actual card details and requires a security check for every purchase, while preserving existing card rewards and protections for eligible disputes.
Built in partnership with American Express, Mastercard, and Visa, ChatGPT Wallet will initially be available through dots for ChatGPT Pro subscribers in the US. Alongside ChatGPT Wallet, we’re releasing tools and guidance to help businesses support customers using agents.
For developers and businesses, ChatGPT Wallet is designed to work with existing commerce infrastructure. Existing checkout pages should work without a Wallet-specific integration, while teams can improve reliability by:
Allowing verified ChatGPT cloud-browser requests using Web Bot Auth
Configuring fraud systems to recognize legitimate agent purchases and relevant Forwarded header signals
Building MCP-based plugins for product discovery, availability, carts, and checkout
Providing a continue_url when a transaction needs to move from a plugin into the browser

Helpful that the launch spells out the merchant side. For anyone wondering how often big retailers block agents in writing: on Nov 9 I read the public robots.txt files at 48 large US retail and marketplace sites. 44 were readable. Only Amazon fully disallows ChatGPT-User (along with GPTBot, OAI-SearchBot and the Claude and Perplexity tokens). Instacart disallows User-agent: * for the whole site. 29 of the 44, including Walmart, Target, Costco and Home Depot, don’t name any of the 14 AI crawlers or agent tokens I track.
So written blocks are rare. The bigger risk for Wallet is probably the one the Accept payments guide describes: bot checks and fraud rules tripping on the cloud browser, which robots.txt can’t show.
A question for the OpenAI team: does the dots cloud browser identify itself with the ChatGPT-User token, or only through Web Bot Auth signatures? That changes which rule a store owner should check.
I re-read these files weekly and publish the table free (search “Agent Shopping Tracker who blocks AI shopping agents”). Disclosure: it’s my own site.
